basic_identification.full_title: Polyaluminium Chloride for Treatment of Water, Sewage and Industrial Effluents — Specification
basic_identification.sector_category: Chemical (approved by the Chemical Division Council of the Bureau of Indian Standards)

scope.summary: This standard prescribes the requirements and the methods of sampling and test for polyaluminium chloride used for the treatment of drinking water, sewage, and industrial effluents [1]. It covers both liquid and powder forms of the chemical across medium and high basicity classifications.

certification_and_marking.certification_status: Certification under the BIS Standard Mark scheme is permissive (voluntary) according to the text of the specification [4]. While polyaluminium chloride does not carry a mandatory standard marking requirement in the code text, the specification mandates clear container labeling, detailed physical and chemical composition tests, and strict consent clearances for carrying the optional ECO-Mark [5, 6].

requirements.detail: The polyaluminium chloride conforming to the requirements of this standard may be certified under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016, and marked with the Standard Mark [4].

Each container or drum must be legibly and indelibly marked with: the product name and type (Liquid/Powder, and Medium/High Basicity), manufacturer name or trade-mark, net quantity, batch/lot number, month and year of manufacture, total Al2O3 percentage by mass, and the clear notice 'For Water Treatment' [4].

To carry the combined Standard and ECO-Mark, the manufacturer must produce official consent clearances from the State Pollution Control Board under the Water Act, 1974 and Air Act, 1981 [6]. Furthermore, the product must satisfy strict trace limits for heavy metals (such as Mercury, Cadmium, Arsenic, Lead) and the packaging must use recyclable, biodegradable, or reusable materials [5, 6].

Batch evaluation must verify that chemical parameters strictly satisfy specified limits: minimum Aluminium as Al2O3 of 9.5% (liquid) / 28.0% (powder); relative basicity of 35% minimum (medium) / 64% minimum (high); maximum total organic carbon (TOC) of 80 ppm (liquid) / 240 ppm (powder); and maximum pH ranges of 1.8-4.5 (liquid) / 2.5-4.5 (powder) for a 5 percent solution.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 15573:2018 is the national Indian Standard specification for Polyaluminium Chloride (PAC) used to treat drinking water, sewage, and industrial waste effluents. It categorizes PAC into liquid and powder forms, subdivided into medium and high basicity grades based on relative alkalinity. When sourcing and inspecting this chemical, engineers must verify key physical and chemical characteristics, including minimum Al2O3 concentration (9.5% for liquid, 28% for powder), relative basicity (minimum 35% or 64%), dynamic viscosity limits, and strict maximum limits on toxic heavy metals (such as Lead, Cadmium, Mercury, and Arsenic) to ensure high-performance, non-toxic water purification.
